title: Duals and pullback comparison for finite near-projective modules
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $J\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $M$ a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose that for each $a\in J$ there are an integer $r_a\geq0$ and maps $f_a:M\to A^{\oplus r_a}$, $g_a:A^{\oplus r_a}\to M$ with $g_af_a=a\operatorname{id}_M$. Then $N=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,A)$ is finite, and each $a\in J$ acts on $N$ through a finite free $A$-module. For any scheme $Z$ [def-pc-scheme] and morphism $g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, put $P=g^*\widetilde M$ and $F=g^*\widetilde N$, using associated module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-associated-module] and ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $G=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Z}(P,\mathcal O_Z)$, the sheaf whose sections on $U\subseteq Z$ are $\mathcal O_U$-linear maps $P|_U\to\mathcal O_U$. The canonical comparison
$$\alpha:F\longrightarrow G$$
is induced by evaluation: locally $(b\otimes\lambda)(b'\otimes m)=bb'\,g^\sharp(\lambda(m))$. Both $\ker\alpha$ and $\operatorname{coker}\alpha$, formed in module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], are annihilated by the extended ideal $J\mathcal O_Z$. For every $m\in M$, evaluation of $\alpha$ at the pulled-back section $m$ equals the pullback of $N\to A$, $\lambda\mapsto\lambda(m)$. No flatness assumption on $g$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose generators $x_1,\ldots,x_s$ of $M$. The map $N\to A^{\oplus s}$, $\lambda\mapsto(\lambda(x_j))_j$, is injective: a functional zero on the generators is zero on every $\sum_jb_jx_j$. Its image is an $A$-submodule of the finite module $A^{\oplus s}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] this image is finite. Transporting its finite generators along the injection proves that $N$ is finite.

Fix $a\in J$ and a factorization $M\xrightarrow{f}A^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{g_a}M$ with $g_af=a\operatorname{id}_M$. For the standard basis write $m_i=g_a(e_i)$ and $\lambda_i=\operatorname{pr}_i\circ f\in N$. Thus $\sum_i\lambda_i(m)m_i=am$ for every $m\in M$. For every $\lambda\in N$ it follows, by evaluation on $m$, that $\sum_i\lambda(m_i)\lambda_i=a\lambda$. Consequently the maps $N\to A^{\oplus r}$, $\lambda\mapsto(\lambda(m_i))_i$, and $A^{\oplus r}\to N$, $(c_i)_i\mapsto\sum_ic_i\lambda_i$, compose to multiplication by $a$. This proves the asserted finite-free factorization on $N$.

source.place: Tag 0G96, lemma-dual-near-projective, taking duals of a finite-free factorization

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-module-pullback], with $S=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$, $P$ and $F$ are canonically the associated sheaves of $S\otimes_A M$ and $S\otimes_A N$, respectively; the comparison sends pulled-back sections to $1\otimes m$ and $1\otimes\lambda$. The same description holds after restricting to any open $U$: apply that lemma to $g|_U$, using the composition law of [def-pc-module-pullback]. The construction in [def-weil-pbc-associated-module] and the bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-associated-module-hom] imply that an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map out of either restricted sheaf is determined by its values on the sections $1\otimes m$ or $1\otimes\lambda$: their $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Z)$-linear span is the corresponding tensor module. In these descriptions the prescribed evaluation comparison is $\alpha_U(b\otimes\lambda)(b^{\prime}\otimes m)=bb^{\prime}g^\sharp(\lambda(m))$. The displayed pairing is balanced over $A$ and linear over $\mathcal O_Z$; for a fixed $\lambda$ it therefore defines a map $P\to\mathcal O_Z$ by the cited associated-sheaf Hom bijection. These maps are $A$-linear in $\lambda$, so the same bijection for $F$ constructs $\alpha:F\to G$. Restriction uses the same formula, proving that this construction is the stated comparison.

proof.text: For the fixed $a$ and the coordinates of Step 2, denote the pulled-back sections by $\bar m_i$ and $\bar\lambda_i$. Define on every open $U$ an $\mathcal O_Z(U)$-linear map $\beta_U:G(U)\to F(U)$ by $\beta_U(\varphi)=\sum_i\varphi_U(\bar m_i|_U)\bar\lambda_i|_U$. This formula commutes with restriction, since $\varphi$ is a morphism of restricted sheaves and all the displayed global sections restrict compatibly. Hence it defines a sheaf morphism $\beta:G\to F$. For any $m\in M$, $\alpha_U(\beta_U(\varphi))$ evaluated on $\bar m|_U$ equals $\sum_i\varphi_U(\bar m_i)g^\sharp(\lambda_i(m))=\varphi_U(\overline{\sum_i\lambda_i(m)m_i})=g^\sharp(a)\varphi_U(\bar m)$. The determination of sheaf maps by these sections from Step 3, applied on every subopen of $U$, gives $\alpha\beta=a\operatorname{id}_G$.

source.place: Tag 0GAB, remark-duals, the finite-free factorization argument, expanded in coordinates for an arbitrary scheme over Spec A

proof.text: For $\lambda\in N$, evaluate the other composite on its pulled-back section: $\beta\alpha(\bar\lambda)=\sum_i g^\sharp(\lambda(m_i))\bar\lambda_i=\overline{\sum_i\lambda(m_i)\lambda_i}=a\bar\lambda$, by Step 2. By the determination of maps out of $F$ in Step 3 this proves $\beta\alpha=a\operatorname{id}_F$. Therefore for a section $v\in\ker\alpha$ we have $av=\beta\alpha(v)=0$. For a section $w\in G$ we have $aw=\alpha\beta(w)$, so multiplication by $a$ on the sectionwise quotient $G/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is zero and remains zero after sheafification. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], that sheafification is the cokernel. This holds for every $a\in J$, so local finite sums of their $\mathcal O_Z$-multiples also annihilate both sheaves: the annihilator contains $J\mathcal O_Z$.

source.place: Tag 0GAB, remark-duals, the finite-free factorization argument, expanded in coordinates for an arbitrary scheme over Spec A

proof.text: For fixed $m\in M$, evaluation of $\alpha$ on $\bar m$ sends $b\otimes\lambda$ to $b\,g^\sharp(\lambda(m))$. The pullback of the map $N\to A$, $\lambda\mapsto\lambda(m)$, has exactly this formula by the naturality and normalized section formula in [lem-weil-pbc-associated-module-pullback]. Equality on these sections determines equality on $F$ as in Step 3. This proves the final compatibility. Every construction used ordinary tensor pullback, and none used preservation of injections by tensoring.

lean.statement: theorem nearProjective_dual_comparison (A : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsNoetherianRing A] (J : Ideal A) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) [Module.Finite A M] (hM : ∀ a ∈ J, ∃ (r : ℕ) (f : M →ₗ[A] (Fin r → A)) (h : (Fin r → A) →ₗ[A] M), h.comp f = a • LinearMap.id) : Module.Finite A (Module.Dual A M) ∧ (∀ a ∈ J, ∃ (r : ℕ) (f : Module.Dual A M →ₗ[A] (Fin r → A)) (h : (Fin r → A) →ₗ[A] Module.Dual A M), h.comp f = a • LinearMap.id) ∧ ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ Spec A), ∃! α : pulled A g (ModuleCat.of A (Module.Dual A M)) ⟶ dualSheaf A g M, (∀ (U : Z.Opens) (b b' : Γ(Z, U)) (l : Module.Dual A M) (m : M), PresheafOfModules.homObjEvalId (R := Z.sheaf.obj) (pulled A g M).val (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf).val U (α.app U (b • pulledSection A g (ModuleCat.of A (Module.Dual A M)) U l)) (b' • pulledSection A g M U m) = b * b' * scalar A g U (l m)) ∧ (∀ (U : Z.Opens) (a : A), a ∈ J → ∀ x : Γ(kernel α, U), scalar A g U a • x = 0) ∧ (∀ (U : Z.Opens) (a : A), a ∈ J → ∀ x : Γ(cokernel α, U), scalar A g U a • x = 0) ∧ (∀ (m : M) (U : Z.Opens) (x : Γ(pulled A g (ModuleCat.of A (Module.Dual A M)), U)), PresheafOfModules.homObjEvalId (R := Z.sheaf.obj) (pulled A g M).val (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf).val U (α.app U x) (pulledSection A g M U m) = (pulledEvaluation A g M m).app U x)
